title: Queue file still grows without bound: every operation rewrites the whole file and done/dead jobs are never pruned or archived
evidence: Second half of ISS-JOBQUEUE-002 fix_direction (prune/archive done and dead jobs). The lock closes the lost update; it does not shrink the file or shorten the time the lock is held, which grows with queue size (ISS-JOBQUEUE-002 recorded 5,000 jobs = 1.3 MB, 68 ms enqueue). Not re-measured here.
fix_direction: Prune or archive done/dead jobs older than a retention age inside the locked section; re-measure lock hold time on a 5,000-job file before wiring.

title: Lock guarantee limits: a holder paused longer than lockStaleMs can lose its lock; claim on a missing dir now creates it; same-thread nested calls cannot wait
evidence: By design, documented in the file header: takeover after staleMs (default 30 s) is by rename of the old lock; a holder frozen past that point is caught only by the stillHeld() read immediately before the rename and the content re-read, leaving a few-instruction window. Lock create needs the directory, so an operation that previously only read (claim on a never-created queue dir) now runs mkdirp. No network-filesystem guarantee.
fix_direction: Only if a runner can stall a worker for more than 30 s inside a queue call: raise lockStaleMs or add a heartbeat on the lock. Not needed for short single-machine operations.

title: Queue lock takeover is by age alone (no pid/host liveness): a live holder paused past lockStaleMs is displaced and the last-instruction window still loses an acknowledged write (ISS-LOCKTAKE-005 class)
evidence: Own real-fs repro: fs wrapper runs a second FileJobQueue.enqueue (wallNow +31 s, lockWaitMs 0) exactly at A's tmp->queue rename, i.e. after A's stillHeld() and content re-read passed. Result: A ok 'enqueued', B ok 'enqueued', stored ids [fromA]; B's acknowledged job is lost. Reachable only if a live holder stalls >30 s between its re-read and the rename (GC, AV scan, CPU starvation); the run-state lock (run-state-lock.ts) never displaces a live same-host pid below a 1 h ceiling.
fix_direction: Record pid+host in the lock body and skip takeover while the pid is alive (reuse the run-state judge), or heartbeat the lock; the rename-time window cannot be closed by a re-check alone.
class: data write, narrowed but not closed; outside the maker's stated guarantee

title: Windows EPERM/EBUSY on lock create or read (delete-pending lock) is returned as io-error, not retried and not typed conflict
evidence: Own stress, 4 child processes x 25 enqueues on one dir (real fs, Windows): lockWait 20 s 100/100 stored, 0 errors; lockWait 2 s 1 of 100 attempts failed with io-error 'EPERM: operation not permitted, open ...'; lockWait 100 ms 2 of 100 io-error EPERM plus 23 conflict. No acknowledged write was lost and nothing was written by the failed call, but a non-conflicting writer gets an error the caller cannot tell from a real I/O fault, contrary to the stated 'cannot get the lock -> typed conflict'.
fix_direction: Treat EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY on lock create/read as contention (retry within the wait budget, then conflict), as run-state-lock.ts createFile does.
class: availability of data write path, no loss
